#ifndef UXB_MIR_X64_TYPED_LOCALS_FBS
#define UXB_MIR_X64_TYPED_LOCALS_FBS

#include once "../../semantic/mir_model.fbs"
#include once "../../semantic/mir_var_info.fbs"
#include once "../../semantic/mir_type_layout_bridge.fbs"
#include once "mir_x64_context.fbs"
#include once "mir_x64_emit_helpers.fbs"
#include once "mir_x64_register_allocator.fbs"

Function MIRX64FindTypedLocalInfo(ByRef fn As MIRFunction, ByVal nameText As String) As Integer
    Dim key As String
    key = UCase(Trim(nameText))

    Dim i As Integer
    For i = 0 To fn.localVarCount - 1
        If UCase(Trim(fn.localVars(i))) = key Then Return i
    Next i

    For i = 0 To fn.paramVarCount - 1
        If UCase(Trim(fn.paramVars(i))) = key Then Return -(i + 1)
    Next i

    Return 999999
End Function

Function MIRX64TypeNameForVar(ByRef fn As MIRFunction, ByVal nameText As String) As String
    Dim idx As Integer
    idx = MIRX64FindTypedLocalInfo(fn, nameText)

    Dim typeName As String
    If idx >= 0 And idx < fn.localVarCount Then
        typeName = MIRCanonicalTypeName2(fn.localVarTypes(idx))
    ElseIf idx < 0 Then
        Dim paramIndex As Integer
        paramIndex = -idx - 1
        If paramIndex >= 0 And paramIndex < fn.paramVarCount Then
            typeName = MIRCanonicalTypeName2(fn.paramVarTypes(paramIndex))
        End If
    End If

    If Left(typeName, 5) = "TYPE_" Then typeName = Mid(typeName, 6)
    Return UCase(Trim(typeName))
End Function

Function MIRX64StackSlotBytesForVar(ByRef fn As MIRFunction, ByVal nameText As String) As Integer
    Dim typeName As String
    typeName = MIRX64TypeNameForVar(fn, nameText)
    If typeName = "" Then Return 0

    Dim typeInfo As MIRTypeInfo
    typeInfo = MIRTypeInfoFromName(typeName)
    Return MIRStackSlotBytes(typeInfo)
End Function

Function MIRX64EnsureTypedLocalSlot( _
    ByRef cg As MIRX64Context, _
    ByRef fn As MIRFunction, _
    ByVal nameText As String, _
    ByRef offsetOut As Integer _
) As Integer

    Dim key As String
    key = UCase(Trim(nameText))
    If key = "" Then Return 0

    If MIRX64FindLocalOffset(cg, key, offsetOut) <> 0 Then Return 1

    Dim idx As Integer
    idx = cg.localCount

    If cg.localCount = 0 Then
        ReDim cg.locals(0)
    Else
        ReDim Preserve cg.locals(cg.localCount)
    End If
    cg.localCount += 1

    cg.locals(idx).nameText = key
    cg.locals(idx).typeName = MIRX64TypeNameForVar(fn, key)
    If cg.locals(idx).typeName = "" Then Return 0
    cg.locals(idx).sizeBytes = MIRX64StackSlotBytesForVar(fn, key)
    If cg.locals(idx).sizeBytes <= 0 Then Return 0
    cg.locals(idx).offset = MIRX64LocalSlotOffset(idx)

    offsetOut = cg.locals(idx).offset
    Return 1
End Function

Function MIRX64CollectTypedLocals(ByRef fn As MIRFunction, ByRef cg As MIRX64Context, ByRef errText As String) As Integer
    Dim i As Integer
    Dim off As Integer

    For i = 0 To fn.paramVarCount - 1
        If MIRX64EnsureTypedLocalSlot(cg, fn, fn.paramVars(i), off) = 0 Then
            errText = "MIR x64 typed locals: param slot failed: " & fn.paramVars(i)
            Return 0
        End If
    Next i

    For i = 0 To fn.localVarCount - 1
        If MIRX64EnsureTypedLocalSlot(cg, fn, fn.localVars(i), off) = 0 Then
            errText = "MIR x64 typed locals: local slot failed: " & fn.localVars(i)
            Return 0
        End If
    Next i

    cg.stackBytes = MIRX64StackBytesForLocals(cg.localCount)
    Return 1
End Function

    ByRef sourceReg As String, _

Private Function MIRInvokeRoutineNoArg(ByRef state As MIREvaluatorState, ByRef routineNameRaw As String, ByRef ret As MIRValue, ByRef errMsg As String) As Integer
    Dim routineName As String
    routineName = UCase(Trim(routineNameRaw))
    If routineName = "" Then
        errMsg = "MIR: slot lane routine is empty"
        Return 0
    End If

    Dim fnIdx As Integer
    fnIdx = MIRFindFunctionIndex(state.module, routineName)
    If fnIdx = -1 Then
        errMsg = "MIR: slot lane routine not found " & routineName
        Return 0
    End If

    Dim savedInstr As MIRIRInstruction
    savedInstr = gMirInstr

    Dim callInstr As MIRIRInstruction
    callInstr.opcode = MIR_OP_CALL
    callInstr.operandCount = 1
    callInstr.operands(0) = routineName
    callInstr.result = ""
    gMirInstr = callInstr

    Dim ok As Integer
    ok = MIRInvokeUserFunction(state, fnIdx, ret, errMsg)
    gMirInstr = savedInstr
    Return ok
End Function

Private Function MIRSlotTriggerEntry(ByRef state As MIREvaluatorState, ByVal entryIdx As Integer, ByVal pipeInputReady As Integer, ByRef pipeInput As MIRValue, ByVal pipeOutputWanted As Integer, ByRef ret As MIRValue, ByRef errMsg As String) As Integer
    If entryIdx < 0 Or entryIdx >= gMirSlotEntryCount Then
        errMsg = "MIR: slot target not found"
        Return 0
    End If

    If gMirSlotEntries(entryIdx).active = 0 Then
        ret.valueType = "INTEGER"
        ret.intValue = 0
        Return 1
    End If

    If pipeInputReady <> 0 Then
        MIRSetVarValue state, "INPUT", pipeInput
    End If

    If pipeOutputWanted <> 0 Then
        Dim zeroOut As MIRValue
        zeroOut.valueType = "INTEGER"
        zeroOut.intValue = 0
        zeroOut.floatValue = 0
        zeroOut.stringValue = ""
        zeroOut.arrayId = -1
        zeroOut.arrayLower = 0
        zeroOut.arraySize = 0
        MIRSetVarValue state, "OUTPUT", zeroOut
    End If

    If MIRInvokeRoutineNoArg(state, gMirSlotEntries(entryIdx).routineName, ret, errMsg) = 0 Then Return 0

    If pipeOutputWanted <> 0 Then
        If MIRGetVarValue(state, "OUTPUT", ret) = 0 Then
            ret.valueType = "INTEGER"
            ret.intValue = 0
            ret.floatValue = 0
            ret.stringValue = ""
            ret.arrayId = -1
            ret.arrayLower = 0
            ret.arraySize = 0
        End If
    End If

    Return 1
End Function

Private Function MIRTryInvokeSlotByCallName(ByRef state As MIREvaluatorState, ByRef fnName As String, ByRef arg1 As MIRValue, ByVal hasArg1 As Integer, ByRef ret As MIRValue, ByRef handledOut As Integer, ByRef errMsg As String) As Integer
    handledOut = 0

' Split tail orchestrator
' Extracted tail for mir_evaluator modular split

' True only for a CALL argument that names a real, writable storage location
' (a plain identifier) rather than a literal or a sub-expression result. Used
' to decide which BYREF arguments get their final value written back into the
' caller's variable after the call returns -- mirrors the same "only plain
' IDENT arguments get BYREF treatment" rule used by the AST interpreter
' (exec_call_dispatch_helpers.fbs) and the x64 backend (MIRX64IsLikelyVariableToken).
Private Function MIRIsLikelyVariableArgToken(ByRef tokenText As String) As Integer
    Dim t As String
    t = Trim(tokenText)
    If t = "" Then Return 0

    ' Anything MIRValueFromString recognizes (integer/float literal, quoted
    ' string, TRUE/FALSE) is a literal, not a writable variable.
    Dim probe As MIRValue
    If MIRValueFromString(t, probe) <> 0 Then Return 0

    Dim i As Integer
    For i = 1 To Len(t)
        Dim c As Integer
        c = Asc(Mid(t, i, 1))
        If c = 95 Then Continue For
        If c >= 48 And c <= 57 Then Continue For
        If c >= 65 And c <= 90 Then Continue For
        If c >= 97 And c <= 122 Then Continue For
        Return 0
    Next i

    Return 1
End Function

Private Function MIRInvokeUserFunction(ByRef state As MIREvaluatorState, ByVal fnIdx As Integer, ByRef ret As MIRValue, ByRef errMsg As String) As Integer
    Dim fn As MIRFunction
    If fnIdx < 0 Or fnIdx >= state.module.functionCount Then
        errMsg = "MIR: CALL function index out of range"
        Return 0
    End If
    fn = state.module.functions(fnIdx)

    Dim argCount As Integer
    argCount = gMirInstr.operandCount - 1
    If argCount < 0 Then argCount = 0

    If argCount <> fn.paramVarCount Then
        errMsg = "MIR: CALL arguman sayisi uyusmuyor " & fn.name & " expected=" & LTrim(Str(fn.paramVarCount)) & " actual=" & LTrim(Str(argCount))
        Return 0
    End If

    Dim argValues(Any) As MIRValue
    If argCount > 0 Then ReDim argValues(argCount - 1)

    ' Non-empty only for a BYREF parameter whose call-site argument is a plain
    ' variable -- captured here (while the raw operand text is still at hand)
    ' so the final value can be written back into that caller variable after
    ' the call returns.
    Dim callerArgNames(Any) As String
    If argCount > 0 Then ReDim callerArgNames(argCount - 1)

    Dim i As Integer
    For i = 0 To argCount - 1
        If MIRTryGetCallArg(state, i, argValues(i)) = 0 Then
            Dim rawArgText As String
            rawArgText = ""
            If gMirInstr.operandCount >= i + 2 Then rawArgText = gMirInstr.operands(i + 1)
            errMsg = "MIR: CALL arguman cozumlene medi fn=" & fn.name & " index=" & LTrim(Str(i)) & " raw=" & rawArgText
            Return 0
        End If
        If i < UBound(fn.paramByRef) + 1 AndAlso fn.paramByRef(i) <> 0 AndAlso gMirInstr.operandCount >= i + 2 Then
            Dim byRefRawArgText As String
            byRefRawArgText = gMirInstr.operands(i + 1)
            If MIRIsLikelyVariableArgToken(byRefRawArgText) <> 0 Then callerArgNames(i) = byRefRawArgText
        End If
    Next i

    Dim savedFunction As Integer
    Dim savedBlock As Integer
    Dim savedInstruction As Integer
    Dim savedExitRequested As Integer
    savedFunction = state.currentFunction
    savedBlock = state.currentBlock
    savedInstruction = state.currentInstruction
    savedExitRequested = state.exitRequested

    Dim hadResultVar As Integer
    Dim oldResultVar As MIRValue
    hadResultVar = MIRGetVarValue(state, "__result__", oldResultVar)

    Dim zeroValue As MIRValue
    zeroValue.valueType = "INTEGER"
    zeroValue.intValue = 0
    zeroValue.floatValue = 0
    zeroValue.stringValue = ""
    zeroValue.arrayId = -1
    zeroValue.arrayLower = 0
    zeroValue.arraySize = 0
    MIRSetVarValue state, "__result__", zeroValue

    Dim hadParam(Any) As Integer
    Dim oldParam(Any) As MIRValue
    If fn.paramVarCount > 0 Then
        ReDim hadParam(fn.paramVarCount - 1)
        ReDim oldParam(fn.paramVarCount - 1)
    End If

    For i = 0 To fn.paramVarCount - 1
        hadParam(i) = MIRGetVarValue(state, fn.paramVars(i), oldParam(i))

        ' Bind the argument as the parameter's DECLARED type, not as whatever
        ' width the caller happened to produce -- otherwise "value AS I8"
        ' receiving 255 keeps 255 here while the AST interpreter yields -1.
        ' A BYREF parameter carries the caller's own storage and must not be
        ' reshaped on entry; non-scalar types (STRING, arrays, objects) report
        ' "not applicable" and pass through untouched.
        Dim boundValue As MIRValue
        boundValue = argValues(i)
        If i > UBound(fn.paramByRef) OrElse fn.paramByRef(i) = 0 Then
            If i <= UBound(fn.paramVarTypes) Then
                MIRApplyDeclaredScalarType boundValue, fn.paramVarTypes(i)
            End If
        End If

        MIRSetVarValue state, fn.paramVars(i), boundValue
    Next i

    state.currentFunction = fnIdx
    state.currentBlock = fn.entryBlock
    state.currentInstruction = 0
    state.exitRequested = 0

    Dim stepGuard As Integer
    stepGuard = 0

    Do While state.exitRequested = 0
        stepGuard += 1
        If stepGuard > 200000 Then
            errMsg = "MIR: function execution guard exceeded: " & fn.name
            Exit Do
        End If

        If state.currentFunction < 0 Or state.currentFunction >= state.module.functionCount Then
            errMsg = "MIR: current function index out of range"
            Exit Do
        End If

        Dim runFn As MIRFunction
        runFn = state.module.functions(state.currentFunction)
        If runFn.blockCount <= 0 Then
            state.exitRequested = 1
            Exit Do
        End If

        If state.currentBlock < 0 Or state.currentBlock >= runFn.blockCount Then
            errMsg = "MIR: current block index out of range"
            Exit Do
        End If

        Dim blk As MIRBasicBlock
        blk = runFn.blocks(state.currentBlock)

        If state.currentInstruction < 0 Then state.currentInstruction = 0
        If state.currentInstruction >= blk.instructionCount Then
            If blk.successorCount > 0 Then
                state.currentBlock = blk.successors(0)
                state.currentInstruction = 0
                Continue Do
            End If
            state.exitRequested = 1
            Exit Do
        End If

        gMirInstr = blk.instructions(state.currentInstruction)
        If MIREvaluateInstruction(state, errMsg) = 0 Then Exit Do

        If state.exitRequested = 0 Then
            state.currentInstruction += 1
        End If
    Loop

    Dim callErr As String
    callErr = errMsg

    If callErr = "" Then
        If MIRGetVarValue(state, "__result__", ret) = 0 Then
            If MIRGetVarValue(state, fn.name, ret) = 0 Then
                ret = zeroValue
            End If
        End If
    End If

    ' Capture each BYREF parameter's final value BEFORE the restore loop below
    ' overwrites the parameter's slot back to its pre-call value -- this also
    ' covers the (unusual but possible, since this interpreter uses one flat
    ' variable table) case where the caller's argument happens to share the
    ' exact same name as the callee's own parameter.
    Dim byRefFinalValues(Any) As MIRValue
    If fn.paramVarCount > 0 Then ReDim byRefFinalValues(fn.paramVarCount - 1)
    For i = 0 To fn.paramVarCount - 1
        If i < UBound(fn.paramByRef) + 1 AndAlso fn.paramByRef(i) <> 0 AndAlso Trim(callerArgNames(i)) <> "" Then
            MIRGetVarValue state, fn.paramVars(i), byRefFinalValues(i)
        End If
    Next i

    For i = 0 To fn.paramVarCount - 1
        If hadParam(i) <> 0 Then
            MIRSetVarValue state, fn.paramVars(i), oldParam(i)
        Else
            MIRSetVarValue state, fn.paramVars(i), zeroValue
        End If
    Next i

    For i = 0 To fn.paramVarCount - 1
        If i < UBound(fn.paramByRef) + 1 AndAlso fn.paramByRef(i) <> 0 AndAlso Trim(callerArgNames(i)) <> "" Then
            MIRSetVarValue state, callerArgNames(i), byRefFinalValues(i)
        End If
    Next i

    If hadResultVar <> 0 Then
        MIRSetVarValue state, "__result__", oldResultVar
    Else
        MIRSetVarValue state, "__result__", zeroValue
    End If

    state.currentFunction = savedFunction
    state.currentBlock = savedBlock
    state.currentInstruction = savedInstruction
    state.exitRequested = savedExitRequested

    If callErr <> "" Then
        errMsg = callErr
        Return 0
    End If

    Return 1
End Function

' ABI10_MIR_BLOCK_LABEL_FIX_20260706: canonical MIR CALL can target a user FUNCTION/SUB
    ' label produced by the semantic bridge.  Bind call operands to parameter names stored on
    ' the function label, execute the routine, and copy the return value into resultName.
    If canonicalCallOp = "MIR_METHOD_CALL" Or canonicalCallOp = "MIR_VIRTUAL_CALL" Or UXBMIRInterpIsFfiCall(ins) = 0 Then
        Dim userRoutineIdx As Integer
        userRoutineIdx = UXBMIRInterpFindLabel(st, callName)
        If userRoutineIdx >= 0 And userRoutineIdx < instructionCount Then
            handledOut = 1
            UXBMIRInterpEnterScope st
            Dim userLabel As UXBMIRInstructionRecord
            userLabel = instructions(userRoutineIdx)
            Dim userParamCount As Integer
            userParamCount = userLabel.operandCount - 1
            If userParamCount < 0 Then userParamCount = 0
            ' Non-empty only for a BYREF parameter (see UXB_MIR_CANONICAL_BYREF_PARAM_PREFIX)
            ' whose call-site argument is a plain writable variable -- used below to write
            ' the parameter's final value back into that caller variable.
            Dim byRefParamNames(Any) As String
            Dim byRefCallerArgNames(Any) As String
            If userParamCount > 0 Then
                ReDim byRefParamNames(userParamCount - 1)
                ReDim byRefCallerArgNames(userParamCount - 1)
            End If

            Dim userParamIdx As Integer
            For userParamIdx = 0 To userParamCount - 1
                If userParamIdx + 1 > 15 Then Exit For
                Dim userParamNameRaw As String
                userParamNameRaw = Trim(userLabel.operands(userParamIdx + 1))
                Dim userParamIsByRef As Integer
                userParamIsByRef = 0
                Dim userParamName As String
                userParamName = userParamNameRaw
                If Left(userParamNameRaw, Len(UXB_MIR_CANONICAL_BYREF_PARAM_PREFIX)) = UXB_MIR_CANONICAL_BYREF_PARAM_PREFIX Then
                    userParamIsByRef = 1
                    userParamName = Mid(userParamNameRaw, Len(UXB_MIR_CANONICAL_BYREF_PARAM_PREFIX) + 1)
                End If
                If userParamName <> "" Then
                    Dim userArgValue As UXBInterpValue
                    userArgValue = UXBInterpValueVoid()
                    Dim sourceOperandIndex As Integer
                    If canonicalCallOp = "MIR_METHOD_CALL" Or canonicalCallOp = "MIR_VIRTUAL_CALL" Then
                        If userParamIdx = 0 Then
                            sourceOperandIndex = 1
                        Else
                            sourceOperandIndex = userParamIdx + 3
                        End If
                    Else
                        sourceOperandIndex = userParamIdx + 1
                    End If
                    If ins.operandCount > sourceOperandIndex Then userArgValue = UXBMIRInterpGetOperand(st, ins.operands(sourceOperandIndex))
                    UXBMIRInterpSetVar st, userParamName, userArgValue
                    If userParamIsByRef <> 0 And ins.operandCount > sourceOperandIndex Then
                        Dim callerArgRaw As String
                        callerArgRaw = Trim(ins.operands(sourceOperandIndex))
                        If UXBMIRInterpIsReferenceName(callerArgRaw) <> 0 Then
                            byRefParamNames(userParamIdx) = userParamName
                            byRefCallerArgNames(userParamIdx) = callerArgRaw
                        End If
                    End If
                End If
            Next userParamIdx
            Dim userInvokeErr As String
            Dim userInvokeValue As UXBInterpValue
            userInvokeValue = UXBMIRInterpInvokeLabel(instructions(), instructionCount, ctx, st, callName, userInvokeErr)

            ' Capture each BYREF parameter's final value BEFORE leaving the callee's
            ' scope discards it, then write it into the caller's variable AFTER
            ' leaving -- so a caller variable that happens to share its name with
            ' the callee's own parameter ends up with the callee's result, not a
            ' stale shadowed copy.
            Dim byRefFinalValues(Any) As UXBInterpValue
            If userParamCount > 0 Then ReDim byRefFinalValues(userParamCount - 1)
            Dim byRefIdx As Integer
            If UXBInterpIsError(userInvokeValue) = 0 Then
                For byRefIdx = 0 To userParamCount - 1
                    If Trim(byRefCallerArgNames(byRefIdx)) <> "" Then
                        byRefFinalValues(byRefIdx) = UXBMIRInterpGetOperand(st, byRefParamNames(byRefIdx))
                    End If
                Next byRefIdx
            End If

            UXBMIRInterpLeaveScope st
            If UXBInterpIsError(userInvokeValue) <> 0 Then Return userInvokeValue

231	    Dim op As String = UXBMIRStep4CanonicalOpcode(ins.opcode)
232	    Select Case op
233	    Case "MIR_CONST", "MIR_LOAD_CONST"
234	        Dim sourceText As String = ""
235	        If ins.operandCount > 0 Then sourceText = ins.operands(0) Else sourceText = ins.resultName
236	        Dim v As UXBInterpValue = UXBInterpValueFromLiteral(sourceText, ins.resultType)
237	        If ins.resultName <> "" And UXBMIRInterpIsReferenceName(ins.resultName) <> 0 Then UXBMIRInterpSetVar st, ins.resultName, v
238	        Return v
239	    Case "MIR_LOCAL_DECL", "MIR_GLOBAL_DECL", "MIR_PARAM_DECL"
240	        If ins.resultName = "" And ins.operandCount >= 3 Then
241	            Dim arrayName As String = Trim(ins.operands(0))
242	            Dim lowerValue As UXBInterpValue = UXBMIRInterpGetOperand(st, ins.operands(1))
243	            Dim upperValue As UXBInterpValue = UXBMIRInterpGetOperand(st, ins.operands(2))
244	            Dim arrayId As Integer = UXBInterpHeapAlloc(ctx.heap, "ARRAY", ins.resultType)
245	            If UXBInterpHeapSetArrayBounds(ctx.heap, arrayId, CInt(lowerValue.intValue), CInt(upperValue.intValue)) = 0 Then
246	                Return UXBInterpValueError(UXB_INTERP_ERR_BAD_ARGUMENT, "invalid array bounds")
247	            End If
248	            Dim arrayValue As UXBInterpValue = UXBInterpValueHandle("ARRAY", arrayId)
249	            UXBMIRInterpSetVar st, arrayName, arrayValue
250	            Return UXBInterpValueVoid()
251	        End If
252	        Dim declValue As UXBInterpValue = UXBInterpValueDefaultForType(ins.resultType)

Function UXBMIRInterpExecStorage(ByRef ins As UXBMIRInstructionRecord, ByRef ctx As UXBInterpContext, ByRef st As UXBMIRInterpState) As UXBInterpValue
    Dim op As String = UXBMIRStep4CanonicalOpcode(ins.opcode)
    Select Case op
    Case "MIR_CONST", "MIR_LOAD_CONST"
        Dim sourceText As String = ""
        If ins.operandCount > 0 Then sourceText = ins.operands(0) Else sourceText = ins.resultName
        Dim v As UXBInterpValue = UXBInterpValueFromLiteral(sourceText, ins.resultType)
        If ins.resultName <> "" And UXBMIRInterpIsReferenceName(ins.resultName) <> 0 Then UXBMIRInterpSetVar st, ins.resultName, v
        Return v
    Case "MIR_LOCAL_DECL", "MIR_GLOBAL_DECL", "MIR_PARAM_DECL"
        If ins.resultName = "" And ins.operandCount >= 3 Then
            Dim arrayName As String = Trim(ins.operands(0))
            Dim lowerValue As UXBInterpValue = UXBMIRInterpGetOperand(st, ins.operands(1))
            Dim upperValue As UXBInterpValue = UXBMIRInterpGetOperand(st, ins.operands(2))
            Dim arrayId As Integer = UXBInterpHeapAlloc(ctx.heap, "ARRAY", ins.resultType)
            If UXBInterpHeapSetArrayBounds(ctx.heap, arrayId, CInt(lowerValue.intValue), CInt(upperValue.intValue)) = 0 Then
                Return UXBInterpValueError(UXB_INTERP_ERR_BAD_ARGUMENT, "invalid array bounds")
            End If
            Dim arrayValue As UXBInterpValue = UXBInterpValueHandle("ARRAY", arrayId)
            UXBMIRInterpSetVar st, arrayName, arrayValue
            Return UXBInterpValueVoid()
        End If
        Dim declValue As UXBInterpValue = UXBInterpValueDefaultForType(ins.resultType)
        If ins.operandCount > 0 Then declValue = UXBInterpApplyDeclaredType(UXBMIRInterpGetOperand(st, ins.operands(0)), ins.resultType)
        UXBMIRInterpSetVar st, ins.resultName, declValue
        Return UXBInterpValueVoid()
    Case "MIR_LOAD_LOCAL", "MIR_LOAD_GLOBAL", "MIR_LOAD"
        Dim nameText As String = ""
        If ins.operandCount > 0 Then nameText = ins.operands(0) Else nameText = ins.resultName
        Dim v As UXBInterpValue = UXBMIRInterpGetOperand(st, nameText)

r.moduleRecord.name = "semantic_mir_bridge"
    r.moduleRecord.functionCount = src.functionCount
    r.moduleRecord.globalCount = src.globalVarCount

    Dim fi As Integer
    For fi = 0 To src.functionCount - 1
        UXBSemanticToCanonicalMIRAddFunction r, src.functions(fi)

        ' YAMA-5 POSTFIX: MIR interpreter tarafinda TASK_TRIGGER ile
        ' __SLOTLANE_* gorev fonksiyonlarina donulebilmesi icin her
        ' fonksiyon basina kanonik label eklenir. MAIN label'i normal
        ' calisma akisini bozmaz; RET gorulunce interpreter cikar.
        Dim fnLabel As UXBMIRInstructionRecord
        ' ABI10_MIR_BLOCK_LABEL_FIX_20260706: labels are executable control targets;
        ' carry the visible label in operand(0) as well as resultName for verifier/interpreter symmetry.
        Dim fnLabelOperandCount As Integer
        fnLabelOperandCount = 1 + src.functions(fi).paramVarCount
        If fnLabelOperandCount > 16 Then fnLabelOperandCount = 16
        fnLabel = UXBMIRInstructionMake("LABEL", src.functions(fi).name, "TYPE_VOID", fnLabelOperandCount, src.functions(fi).name)
        fnLabel.operandTypes(0) = UXB_MIR_TYPE_STRING
        Dim fnParamLabelIdx As Integer
        For fnParamLabelIdx = 0 To src.functions(fi).paramVarCount - 1
            If fnParamLabelIdx + 1 > 15 Then Exit For
            Dim fnParamIsByRef As Integer
            fnParamIsByRef = 0
            If fnParamLabelIdx < UBound(src.functions(fi).paramByRef) + 1 Then fnParamIsByRef = src.functions(fi).paramByRef(fnParamLabelIdx)
            ' MIR_FUNCTION_LABEL operands are plain name strings with no room
            ' for a separate BYREF flag field, so a BYREF parameter's name is
            ' prefixed here; the MIR interpreter (UXBMIRInterpInvokeLabel in
            ' mir_interp.fbs) strips this prefix and writes the parameter's
            ' final value back into the caller's argument variable.
            If fnParamIsByRef <> 0 Then
                fnLabel.operands(fnParamLabelIdx + 1) = UXB_MIR_CANONICAL_BYREF_PARAM_PREFIX & src.functions(fi).paramVars(fnParamLabelIdx)
            Else
                fnLabel.operands(fnParamLabelIdx + 1) = src.functions(fi).paramVars(fnParamLabelIdx)
            End If
            fnLabel.operandTypes(fnParamLabelIdx + 1) = UXB_MIR_TYPE_STRING
        Next fnParamLabelIdx
        fnLabel.sourceAstKind = "MIR_FUNCTION_LABEL"
        fnLabel.sourceAstNode = -1
        fnLabel.blockId = IIf(src.functions(fi).blockCount > 0, src.functions(fi).blocks(0).id, 0)
        fnLabel.mirInstructionId = -1
        UXBSemanticToCanonicalMIRAddInstruction r, fnLabel

        Dim bi As Integer
        For bi = 0 To src.functions(fi).blockCount - 1
            UXBSemanticToCanonicalMIRAddBlock r, src.functions(fi).blocks(bi)

            Dim blockLabelText As String
            blockLabelText = UXBSemanticCanonicalMIRBlockLabelName(fi, src.functions(fi).blocks(bi).id)
            Dim blockLabel As UXBMIRInstructionRecord
            blockLabel = UXBMIRInstructionMake("LABEL", blockLabelText, "TYPE_VOID", 1, blockLabelText)
            blockLabel.operandTypes(0) = UXB_MIR_TYPE_STRING
            blockLabel.sourceAstKind = "MIR_BLOCK_LABEL"
            blockLabel.sourceAstNode = -1
            blockLabel.blockId = src.functions(fi).blocks(bi).id
            blockLabel.mirInstructionId = -1
            UXBSemanticToCanonicalMIRAddInstruction r, blockLabel

            Dim ii As Integer
            For ii = 0 To src.functions(fi).blocks(bi).instructionCount - 1
                Dim canonical As UXBMIRInstructionRecord
                Dim instErr As String
                canonical.mirInstructionId = ii
                If UXBSemanticMIRInstructionToCanonical(src, src.functions(fi).blocks(bi).instructions(ii), canonical, instErr) = 0 Then
                    r.invalidInstructionCount += 1
                    r.diagnosticsText &= "fn=" & src.functions(fi).name & " block=" & LTrim(Str(src.functions(fi).blocks(bi).id)) & " inst=" & LTrim(Str(ii)) & ": " & instErr & Chr(10)
                    If strictVerify <> 0 Then
                        r.verifyStatus = "FAIL"
                        r.moduleRecord.verifyStatus = "FAIL"
                        errText = r.diagnosticsText
                        Return 0
                    End If
                End If
                canonical.mirInstructionId = ii

' Split tail orchestrator
' Extracted tail for mir_evaluator modular split

' True only for a CALL argument that names a real, writable storage location
' (a plain identifier) rather than a literal or a sub-expression result. Used
' to decide which BYREF arguments get their final value written back into the
' caller's variable after the call returns -- mirrors the same "only plain
' IDENT arguments get BYREF treatment" rule used by the AST interpreter
' (exec_call_dispatch_helpers.fbs) and the x64 backend (MIRX64IsLikelyVariableToken).
Private Function MIRIsLikelyVariableArgToken(ByRef tokenText As String) As Integer
    Dim t As String
    t = Trim(tokenText)
    If t = "" Then Return 0

    ' Anything MIRValueFromString recognizes (integer/float literal, quoted
    ' string, TRUE/FALSE) is a literal, not a writable variable.
    Dim probe As MIRValue
    If MIRValueFromString(t, probe) <> 0 Then Return 0

    Dim i As Integer
    For i = 1 To Len(t)
        Dim c As Integer
        c = Asc(Mid(t, i, 1))
        If c = 95 Then Continue For
        If c >= 48 And c <= 57 Then Continue For
        If c >= 65 And c <= 90 Then Continue For
        If c >= 97 And c <= 122 Then Continue For
        Return 0
    Next i

    Return 1
End Function

Private Function MIRInvokeUserFunction(ByRef state As MIREvaluatorState, ByVal fnIdx As Integer, ByRef ret As MIRValue, ByRef errMsg As String) As Integer
    Dim fn As MIRFunction
    If fnIdx < 0 Or fnIdx >= state.module.functionCount Then
        errMsg = "MIR: CALL function index out of range"
        Return 0
    End If
    fn = state.module.functions(fnIdx)

    Dim argCount As Integer
    argCount = gMirInstr.operandCount - 1
    If argCount < 0 Then argCount = 0

    If argCount <> fn.paramVarCount Then
        errMsg = "MIR: CALL arguman sayisi uyusmuyor " & fn.name & " expected=" & LTrim(Str(fn.paramVarCount)) & " actual=" & LTrim(Str(argCount))
        Return 0
    End If

    Dim argValues(Any) As MIRValue
    If argCount > 0 Then ReDim argValues(argCount - 1)

    ' Non-empty only for a BYREF parameter whose call-site argument is a plain
    ' variable -- captured here (while the raw operand text is still at hand)
    ' so the final value can be written back into that caller variable after
    ' the call returns.
    Dim callerArgNames(Any) As String
    If argCount > 0 Then ReDim callerArgNames(argCount - 1)

    Dim i As Integer
    For i = 0 To argCount - 1
        If MIRTryGetCallArg(state, i, argValues(i)) = 0 Then
            Dim rawArgText As String
            rawArgText = ""
            If gMirInstr.operandCount >= i + 2 Then rawArgText = gMirInstr.operands(i + 1)
            errMsg = "MIR: CALL arguman cozumlene medi fn=" & fn.name & " index=" & LTrim(Str(i)) & " raw=" & rawArgText
            Return 0
        End If
        If i < UBound(fn.paramByRef) + 1 AndAlso fn.paramByRef(i) <> 0 AndAlso gMirInstr.operandCount >= i + 2 Then
            Dim byRefRawArgText As String
            byRefRawArgText = gMirInstr.operands(i + 1)
            If MIRIsLikelyVariableArgToken(byRefRawArgText) <> 0 Then callerArgNames(i) = byRefRawArgText
        End If
    Next i

    Dim savedFunction As Integer
    Dim savedBlock As Integer
    Dim savedInstruction As Integer
    Dim savedExitRequested As Integer
    savedFunction = state.currentFunction
    savedBlock = state.currentBlock
    savedInstruction = state.currentInstruction
    savedExitRequested = state.exitRequested

    Dim hadResultVar As Integer
    Dim oldResultVar As MIRValue
    hadResultVar = MIRGetVarValue(state, "__result__", oldResultVar)

    Dim zeroValue As MIRValue
    zeroValue.valueType = "INTEGER"
    zeroValue.intValue = 0
    zeroValue.floatValue = 0
    zeroValue.stringValue = ""
    zeroValue.arrayId = -1
    zeroValue.arrayLower = 0
    zeroValue.arraySize = 0
    MIRSetVarValue state, "__result__", zeroValue

    Dim hadParam(Any) As Integer
    Dim oldParam(Any) As MIRValue
    If fn.paramVarCount > 0 Then
        ReDim hadParam(fn.paramVarCount - 1)
        ReDim oldParam(fn.paramVarCount - 1)
    End If

    For i = 0 To fn.paramVarCount - 1
        hadParam(i) = MIRGetVarValue(state, fn.paramVars(i), oldParam(i))

        ' Bind the argument as the parameter's DECLARED type, not as whatever
        ' width the caller happened to produce -- otherwise "value AS I8"
        ' receiving 255 keeps 255 here while the AST interpreter yields -1.
        ' A BYREF parameter carries the caller's own storage and must not be
        ' reshaped on entry; non-scalar types (STRING, arrays, objects) report
        ' "not applicable" and pass through untouched.
        Dim boundValue As MIRValue
        boundValue = argValues(i)
        Print "DIAG_PARAMBIND fn=" & fn.name & " i=" & Str(i) & " name=" & fn.paramVars(i) & " ubType=" & Str(UBound(fn.paramVarTypes)) & " ubRef=" & Str(UBound(fn.paramByRef)) & " type=[" & fn.paramVarTypes(i) & "] before=" & Str(boundValue.intValue)
        If i > UBound(fn.paramByRef) OrElse fn.paramByRef(i) = 0 Then
            If i <= UBound(fn.paramVarTypes) Then
                MIRApplyDeclaredScalarType boundValue, fn.paramVarTypes(i)
            End If
        End If
        Print "DIAG_PARAMBIND   after=" & Str(boundValue.intValue)

        MIRSetVarValue state, fn.paramVars(i), boundValue
    Next i

    state.currentFunction = fnIdx
    state.currentBlock = fn.entryBlock
    state.currentInstruction = 0
    state.exitRequested = 0

    Dim stepGuard As Integer
    stepGuard = 0

    Do While state.exitRequested = 0
        stepGuard += 1
        If stepGuard > 200000 Then
            errMsg = "MIR: function execution guard exceeded: " & fn.name
            Exit Do
        End If

        If state.currentFunction < 0 Or state.currentFunction >= state.module.functionCount Then
            errMsg = "MIR: current function index out of range"
            Exit Do
        End If

        Dim runFn As MIRFunction
        runFn = state.module.functions(state.currentFunction)
        If runFn.blockCount <= 0 Then
            state.exitRequested = 1
            Exit Do
        End If

        If state.currentBlock < 0 Or state.currentBlock >= runFn.blockCount Then
            errMsg = "MIR: current block index out of range"
            Exit Do
        End If

        Dim blk As MIRBasicBlock
        blk = runFn.blocks(state.currentBlock)

        If state.currentInstruction < 0 Then state.currentInstruction = 0
        If state.currentInstruction >= blk.instructionCount Then
            If blk.successorCount > 0 Then
                state.currentBlock = blk.successors(0)
                state.currentInstruction = 0
                Continue Do
            End If
            state.exitRequested = 1
            Exit Do
        End If

        gMirInstr = blk.instructions(state.currentInstruction)
        If MIREvaluateInstruction(state, errMsg) = 0 Then Exit Do

        If state.exitRequested = 0 Then
            state.currentInstruction += 1
        End If
    Loop

    Dim callErr As String
    callErr = errMsg

    If callErr = "" Then
        If MIRGetVarValue(state, "__result__", ret) = 0 Then
            If MIRGetVarValue(state, fn.name, ret) = 0 Then
                ret = zeroValue
            End If
        End If
    End If

    ' Capture each BYREF parameter's final value BEFORE the restore loop below
    ' overwrites the parameter's slot back to its pre-call value -- this also
    ' covers the (unusual but possible, since this interpreter uses one flat
    ' variable table) case where the caller's argument happens to share the
    ' exact same name as the callee's own parameter.
    Dim byRefFinalValues(Any) As MIRValue
    If fn.paramVarCount > 0 Then ReDim byRefFinalValues(fn.paramVarCount - 1)
    For i = 0 To fn.paramVarCount - 1
        If i < UBound(fn.paramByRef) + 1 AndAlso fn.paramByRef(i) <> 0 AndAlso Trim(callerArgNames(i)) <> "" Then
            MIRGetVarValue state, fn.paramVars(i), byRefFinalValues(i)
        End If
    Next i

    For i = 0 To fn.paramVarCount - 1
        If hadParam(i) <> 0 Then
            MIRSetVarValue state, fn.paramVars(i), oldParam(i)
        Else
            MIRSetVarValue state, fn.paramVars(i), zeroValue
        End If
    Next i

    For i = 0 To fn.paramVarCount - 1
        If i < UBound(fn.paramByRef) + 1 AndAlso fn.paramByRef(i) <> 0 AndAlso Trim(callerArgNames(i)) <> "" Then
            MIRSetVarValue state, callerArgNames(i), byRefFinalValues(i)
        End If
    Next i

    If hadResultVar <> 0 Then
        MIRSetVarValue state, "__result__", oldResultVar
    Else
        MIRSetVarValue state, "__result__", zeroValue
    End If

    state.currentFunction = savedFunction
    state.currentBlock = savedBlock
    state.currentInstruction = savedInstruction
    state.exitRequested = savedExitRequested

    If callErr <> "" Then
        errMsg = callErr
        Return 0
    End If

    Return 1
End Function

#include once "mir_evaluator_tail_controlflow.fbs"
#include once "mir_evaluator_tail_rest.fbs"

`MIRRunModule` hiçbir yerden çağrılmıyor. İlk düzelttiğim yer ölü kod. Durum raporu:

## Adım 2 ve Adım 1 tamamlandı

**Test altyapısı artık gerçekten doğruluyor.** [run_typed_task_tests.ps1](tests/typed_task_routines/run_typed_task_tests.ps1) her pozitif testin çıktısını `expected/` altındaki kayıtlı beklentiyle karşılaştırıyor. AST ve MIR aynı dosyaya bakıyor, yani iki backend'in ayrışması otomatik hata. Negatif testlerde artık sıfırdan farklı çıkış kodu yetmiyor, beklenen tanı mesajının gerçekten çıkması gerekiyor. Eksik beklenti dosyası sessiz geçiş değil, hata.

**Bug düzeldi ve kök nedeni ilk sandığım yer değildi.** Analizim beni önce `mir_evaluator` dosyasına götürdü. Oraya düzeltmeyi yazdım, derledim, hiçbir şey değişmedi. Geçici bir teşhis çıktısı ekleyip ölçtüm: o kod hiç çalışmıyor. `--interpreter-backend MIR` bambaşka bir yol izliyor. Semantic MIR'i canonical MIR'e çeviriyor ve `src/interpreter/mir/` altındaki ayrı bir yorumlayıcıyı çalıştırıyor.

Gerçek neden şuydu: canonical MIR köprüsü fonksiyon etiketinde yalnızca parametre **adlarını** taşıyor. Bildirilen tip yolda kayboluyor. Yorumlayıcı da argümanı ada göre bağlayıp geçiyor.

İyi haber, doğru mekanizma zaten vardı. `MIR_PARAM_DECL` komutunun işleyicisi AST yorumlayıcısının kullandığı `UXBInterpApplyDeclaredType` fonksiyonunu çağırıyor. Sadece bu komut hiç üretilmiyordu. [semantic_to_canonical_mir_bridge.fbs](src/semantic/semantic_to_canonical_mir_bridge.fbs:558) içinde her parametre için bir tane üretiyorum. BYREF parametreler atlanıyor, çünkü onlar çağıranın deposunu paylaşıyor.

x64 tarafında ayrı bir düzeltme gerekti. Üretilen assembly şimdi şöyle:

```asm
mov rax, rcx        ; argüman registeri
movsx rax, al       ; I8'e daralt  <-- yeni
mov qword [rbp-16], rax
```

Önceden ortadaki satır yoktu. Ayrıca normalleştiriciye `BYTE`, `SHORT`, `INTEGER`, `LONG` gibi eş anlamlıları ekledim, yoksa bu adlarla yazılmış parametreler yorumlayıcıda daralıp x64'te daralmayarak yeni bir ayrışma yaratacaktı.

## Doğrulama

| Kontrol | Sonuç |
|---|---|
| Tipli görev testleri | 22 / 22 |
| Aynısı x64 üretimi dahil | 31 / 31 |
| AST ve MIR uyum taraması, 64 test | baseline ile birebir aynı |
| Derleme uyarısı | yok |

Uyum taramasını hem yeni hem de düzeltme öncesi derlemeyle çalıştırdım. Dört kategoride de sayılar aynı çıktı, yani regresyon yok.

## Karar bekleyen üç konu

**Ölü koda yazdığım düzeltmeyi ne yapayım.** `mir_evaluator` dosyalarının yorumlayıcı giriş noktası `MIRRunModule` hiçbir yerden çağrılmıyor. Oraya yazdığım iki değişiklik etkisiz duruyor. Geri almamı öneriyorum. Çalışmayan koda düzeltme bırakmak, ileride okuyanı yanıltır. Yedeği duruyor, geri alması kolay.

**Yedek konusunda bir eksiğim var.** Asıl düzeltmenin girdiği köprü dosyasını yedek listeme almamıştım, çünkü o noktada kök nedenin orada olduğunu bilmiyordum. Eklediğim blok net sınırlı ve geri alınabilir, ama dürüst olmak için söylüyorum.

**Bu iş sırasında bulduğum, benim işimle ilgisiz üç sorun var.** Hiçbirine dokunmadım:

- `47_numeric_casts` testinde `CLNG(2.9)` ve `FIX(5.9)` iki backend'de farklı sonuç veriyor. Ayrı bir builtin bugı. Baseline ile aynı olduğunu doğruladım.
- Altı test MIR'de çalışmıyor, biri görev testi. Sebep bağlanmamış bir runtime servisi, tip sistemi değil.
- Dilin geri kalanı `LONG` tipini 32 bit sayarken, x64 layout köprüsü 64 bit sayıyor. Bu gerçek bir tutarsızlık ama düzeltmek yığın yerleşimini etkiler, ayrı ele alınmalı.

13	**Decisions finalized so far** (from a 3-round interactive Q&A on 2026-09-06, following three prior audit reports on the uxb compiler at `C:\Users\mete\Downloads\BasicOyunSource\UXBc_Clean\UXBc\uxb`):
14	
15	- **Multi-dimensional `DIM`** (currently silently degrades a multi-dim array to a scalar with no error, in `src/semantic/mir_lower_stmt_core_split.fbs`): build full real support, not just a guard error. **DONE for AST interpreter AND MIR/x64 native, empirically verified 2026-09-07** — see the "MIR/x64 native array bug" entry below; multi-dim arrays now produce identical results in both execution forms via a real compiled .exe.
16	- **`BYREF` parameters** (currently a no-op everywhere, always behaves like `BYVAL`): implement it for real, across all four backends (x64, AST/MIR interpreter, JS, WASM). **AST interpreter DONE (2026-09-07, prior session)**: `src/runtime/exec/exec_call_dispatch_helpers.fbs` does copy-in/copy-out BYREF. **MIR/x64 native backend DONE and empirically verified 2026-09-07** via real compiled-and-run .exe files (not just AST interpreter or assembly reading): added `paramByRef` to `MIRFunction`/`MIRX64LocalSlot`, pointer-indirection in every load/store chokepoint (int: `mir_x64_emit_helpers.fbs`; float: `mir_x64_fp64.fbs`), forced-integer-register prologue handling for byref params regardless of declared type (`mir_x64_typed_locals.fbs`), and the call-site fix that actually passes an address instead of a value for byref arguments (`MIRX64EmitUserCallInstruction` in `mir_x64_codegen.fbs`, using `MIRX64AddressOfVarToReg`). Also fixed the related ADDR_OF/LOAD_ADDR edge case (taking the address of a byref parameter now correctly returns the pointer it already holds, not the address of the local copy of that pointer). Verified with mixed BYREF-F64 + BYREF-I32 + BYVAL-F64 test: native x64 output (`toplam=10, adet=2, birDeger_degismemeli=7.5`) matches the AST interpreter exactly. **MIR interpreter (`--interpreter-backend MIR`) DONE and empirically verified 2026-09-07**: important architecture discovery along the way — the codebase has THREE separate interpreter engines, not two: the AST interpreter, `src/semantic/mir_evaluator*.fbs` (a flat-namespace evaluator that turned out to be used only by the YAMA6 slot/event/thread/paralel runtime surface, not by plain `run`), and `src/interpreter/mir/mir_interp.fbs` (a proper scope-stack-based evaluator over a separate "canonical MIR" instruction format) — the THIRD one is what `run --interpreter-backend MIR` actually executes. Implemented BYREF for both: (a) `mir_evaluator_tail.fbs`'s `MIRInvokeUserFunction`, copy-in/copy-out style like the AST interpreter, for completeness even though its real-world exercise path is narrower; (b) the actual one, `mir_interp.fbs`'s `MIREvaluateCallInstruction`, which uses real scope push/pop (`UXBMIRInterpEnterScope`/`LeaveScope`) rather than flat-namespace snapshotting — capture each BYREF parameter's final value from the callee's scope right before `LeaveScope` discards it, then write it into the caller's variable via the scope-chain-aware `UXBMIRInterpAssignVar` right after. This required a genuine format fix too: the canonical-MIR bridge (`semantic_to_canonical_mir_bridge.fbs`) that converts a rich `MIRFunction` (which has `paramByRef`) down into the interpreter's flatter `MIR_FUNCTION_LABEL` instruction format was silently dropping the BYREF flag entirely (that instruction's operands are bare parameter-name strings with no room for it) — fixed by prefixing a BYREF parameter's name with a new shared marker constant (`UXB_MIR_CANONICAL_BYREF_PARAM_PREFIX = "@BYREF@"` in `src/mir/mir_instruction.fbs`) that the interpreter strips off. Verified: both byref test programs AND a broader regression smoke test (struct field access, BYREF-STRING parameter, WHILE loop, multi-dim array) now produce output identical across all three working execution forms (AST interpreter, MIR interpreter, MIR/x64 native). JS / WASM backends still pending — same underlying no-op-BYREF problem remains there until each gets the equivalent fix.
17	- **THREE pre-existing bugs found and fixed while verifying MIR/x64 BYREF (2026-09-07), unrelated to BYREF itself but blocking real end-to-end testing of it:**
18	  1. **`bld`/`--build-x64` silently used the OLD, separate legacy AST-based x64 code generator (`src/codegen/x64/code_generator.fbs`), not the MIR-based one**, unless `--x64-mode=MIR` was explicitly passed on the command line. The `x64`/`--emit-x64-nasm` verb already defaulted to MIR (sets `--x64-mode=MIR` as a CLI alias in `cli_verb_dispatch.fbs`); the `bld` verb dispatch did not set this alias at all, so it silently fell back to the AST emitter (see `main_program_entry.fbs:407-423`'s `x64Mode` default-to-"AST" logic). **This means every previous "verified via bld/exe" claim for MIR-side work (multi-dim arrays included) before 2026-09-07 was actually exercising the OLD AST backend, not the MIR one** — the two backends happen to produce compatible results for plain scalar code, which is why this went unnoticed. **DECIDED AND FIXED 2026-09-07**: user chose to make `bld` default to `--x64-mode=MIR` (matching `x64`/`codegen`) rather than staying AST-default with MIR opt-in — one-line fix in `cli_verb_dispatch.fbs`'s `Case "bld"` (mirrors the existing `Case "x64"` pattern exactly, still overridable with an explicit `--x64-mode=AST`). Re-verified after the flip: BYREF (int/float/mixed), multi-dim arrays, and a broader smoke test (struct field access, BYREF-STRING parameter, WHILE loop, function calls, string/int/float PRINT) all produce output identical to the AST interpreter through the new MIR-default `bld` path. A full sweep of the ~1400-file `tests/` tree was NOT run (impractical scope for this pass) — if something in that tree ever regresses, this default flip is the first thing to suspect.
19	  2. **PRINT of a float value was silently broken in the MIR/x64 native backend**: `MIRX64EmitPrintValue` (`mir_x64_codegen.fbs`) always loaded the operand as an integer and called `__uxb_rt_print_i64`, even for F32/F64 values — printing the raw IEEE-754 bit pattern as a huge garbage integer instead of the actual number. The native runtime (`native/uxb_runtime`) had no float-print export at all. **FIXED**: added `__uxb_rt_print_f64(double)` to `uxb_runtime.h`/`uxb_runtime_mir.cpp` (uses `%g`, matching the legacy AST backend's own float-print format), rebuilt `uxb_runtime.dll` (kept the "full" libuv+tbb variant — do NOT rebuild with `-Variant std`, that silently drops real-concurrency support from the shipped DLL), and wired `MIRX64EmitPrintValue` to check `MIRX64OperandIsFloat` and route through a new `MIRX64EmitRuntimePrintF64` helper.
20	  3. **Arrays (both single- and multi-dimensional) never actually worked through the MIR/x64 native backend at all**, independent of BYREF or the multi-dim work — a general, severe, pre-existing bug. Root cause: a generic "surface keyword" registry (`src/surface/uxb_surface_registry.fbs`, built for keyword-completeness/documentation tracking across all BASIC keywords) recognizes "DIM"/"REDIM" as known keywords and, in `MIRX64TryEmitSurfaceOpcode` (`mir_x64_opcode_surface_emitters.fbs`), its generic `UXBSurfaceKnown(op)` fallback intercepted every DIM/REDIM instruction and silently collapsed it into a no-op generic host-call — before `MIRX64EmitInstruction`'s own array-aware `Case "DIM", "REDIM"` (which calls `MIRX64EmitDimArray` to actually register the array's backing storage) ever got a chance to run. Every `LOAD_INDEXED`/`STORE_INDEXED` then failed with "array not declared" (or, if reached with an empty array table, worse). **FIXED**: added an explicit `Case "DIM", "REDIM"` exemption in `MIRX64TryEmitSurfaceOpcode` (mirroring the pre-existing identical exemption already there for `"CALL"`) so these opcodes fall through to the real handler untouched. Verified with both a plain 1-D array and the 3×4 multi-dim array test, both now produce correct results via a real compiled x64 .exe.
21	- **`FOR EACH` / iterator support** (patch bundle `uXBasic_PATCH5_Iterator_Integration_Hardening_20260809` exists on disk but was never wired into the build — dead code): finish integrating it properly across all backends. **DONE and empirically verified 2026-09-07** for the array case (`FOR EACH x[, idx] IN someArray` / `DO EACH x IN someArray`), across AST interpreter, MIR interpreter, and MIR/x64 native, all producing identical correct output. Before this fix, a single array-variable target silently iterated exactly ONCE with a bogus/zero value instead of walking the array's real elements — the parser and AST shape were already correct, but nothing actually did real per-element iteration. Three separate fixes were needed: (1) wired `MIRLowerArrayEachLoop` (already written in `src/semantic/iterator_lowering.fbs`, PATCH5, but never `#include`d anywhere — confirmed literally zero references to that filename in `src/`) into the existing "Case FOR_EACH_STMT, DO_EACH_STMT" handler in `src/semantic/mir_lower_stmt_core_split.fbs`, trying it first and falling back to the pre-existing "each IN-list item is its own loop pass" legacy semantics (still needed and correctly preserved — e.g. `FOR EACH x IN 1, 2, 3`) only when the target isn't a single statically-bounded array; (2) found and fixed a genuine control-flow bug in that same never-tested PATCH5 code: the loop body's block never jumped to the increment block (`iterator_lowering.fbs` — a missing `MIR_OP_JMP` before `blkIdx = nextBlock`), which is why the earlier symptom was "only the first element gets processed, then the loop just stops" rather than a crash; (3) the AST interpreter (`run`, i.e. `--interpreter-backend AST`) had no array-iteration logic at all — `src/runtime/exec/exec_stmt_flow.fbs`'s `ExecRunForEachStmt`/`ExecRunDoEachStmt` only ever had the legacy per-expression-list behavior — added a parallel `ExecRunSingleArrayEachLoop` there, reusing the existing `ExecGetArrayElement`/`ExecSetVarValue` primitives; since the AST interpreter's arrays are already fully dynamic at runtime (unlike the MIR/x64 static backend), this version also correctly handles a REDIM'd array, which the MIR path explicitly cannot (compile-time bounds only) and deliberately rejects with a clear error instead of guessing. Multi-dimensional array targets are also a deliberate, clearly-erroring scope boundary in both paths (not attempted — no existing design decision for flattened-vs-nested EACH semantics over multi-dim arrays, and the user hasn't been asked). **JS array read/write — FIXED and empirically verified 2026-09-07** (was: "Not yet touched: JS/WASM codegen ... arrayStore target is missing"). Root cause: the JS backend's opcode normalizer (`UXBJsCanonicalOpcode` in `src/codegen/js/js_expr_emit.fbs`) lumped MIR's `DIM` opcode into the same generic `"DECL"` bucket as pure scalar/type declarations, and `UXBJsSurfaceIsMetadata` treats every `"DECL"` as a complete no-op (emits just `;`) — so a `DIM arr(4) AS I32` never actually allocated a JS array; the variable stayed `undefined` forever, and any later `ux.arrayStore`/`arrayLoad` call failed immediately (`arrayStore target is missing`) or silently no-op'd. `REDIM` had the identical class of bug (opcode reached the statement emitter's dispatch but matched no `Case`, silently doing nothing). Fixed by giving `DIM`/`REDIM` their own canonical opcodes and real JS emission in `src/codegen/js/js_stmt_emit.fbs` (`ux.arrayNew(...)` / `ux.arrayResize(...)`), and extended the embedded JS runtime (`src/codegen/js/runtime/js_runtime_embedded_generated.fbs`) so every array object carries its own `__uxbLower` bound (stamped at `arrayNew`/`arrayResize` time), with `arrayLoad`/`arrayStore` subtracting it — this makes non-zero-lower-bound arrays (`DIM arr(1 TO 5)`) correct too, matching x64/AST-interpreter semantics, not just the common 0-based case. `REDIM PRESERVE` is a real implementation (copies old element values into the resized array), not a stub. Verified via real `uxb jsw` compiles run under Node.js: (1) `DIM arr(4) AS I32` + writes + reads + PRINT → `10/20/30`, cross-checked identical against `run` (AST interpreter); (2) `DIM arr(1 TO 5) AS I32` (non-zero lower bound) + `REDIM PRESERVE ... AS I32` on a separate array → `100/500/7/9/42`, all correct. Also did the requested broader scan of `js_runtime_embedded_generated.fbs` for sibling instances of the earlier `""` vs `""""` (2-vs-4-quote) FreeBASIC string-escaping bug class — found no further occurrences beyond the two already fixed earlier this session.

Found by actually running generated JS output under Node.js (`node <file>.js`) rather than just checking that codegen didn't error — worth remembering as a lesson: this file's correctness can't be verified by the compiler's own codegen success/failure, only by executing the JS it produces. This whole embedded-runtime file is clearly a soft spot (hand-escaped multi-hundred-line JS-as-FreeBASIC-string) — see [[uxb-clean-build-effort]] for the earlier related fixes.

Implemented per the user's approved design: FOR EACH snapshots (all keys/values captured before the body runs), DO EACH is JIT (re-reads live each iteration); loop bound (item count) is fixed once at loop entry either way, matching the existing single-array-variable precedent — DO EACH observes value mutations, not count changes, from within the same pass. Second loop variable's meaning is collection-type-driven, not identifier-text-driven (per the approved DICT design decision, option A): LIST/SET -> (item, ordinal index, never physical position, per the approved P4 recommendation); DICT -> (key, value) positionally; DICT single-var binds the key (per the approved decision, matching Python's `for x in dict`).
58	  - New: `ExecEachSingleCollectionVarIdx`/`ExecRunSingleCollectionEachLoop` in `src/runtime/exec/exec_stmt_flow.fbs`, wired into both `ExecRunForEachStmt` and `ExecRunDoEachStmt` (checked after the existing single-array case, before falling back to legacy expression-list semantics). New positional accessors `ExecDictKeyAt`/`ExecDictValueAt`/`ExecSetMemberAt` in `src/runtime/exec/exec_collections.fbs` (insertion order, mirroring the existing `ExecListGet`).
59	  - **P4 implemented too**: `ParseDoEachStmt` (`src/parser/parser/parser_stmt_flow.fbs`) now accepts an optional `, indexVar` second identifier, symmetric with `FOR EACH`'s existing form; `ExecRunDoEachStmt`'s scalar (expression-list) loop now also sets it (was silently ignored before — DO EACH never had an index at all). MIR lowering already handled `st.op` generically for both FOR_EACH_STMT and DO_EACH_STMT (inherited unchanged from the P0 split), so no MIR-lowering change was needed for this part.
60	  - **Four real, pre-existing bugs found and fixed while wiring this up (independent of the FOR EACH feature itself — each was a genuine, exploitable gap the moment anyone actually exercised this code path for the first time):**
61	    1. `src/common/array_memory_ref.fbs:135`, `UXBFindArrayMemoryInfo`: `If typeNode = -1 Or UCase(Trim(ps.ast.nodes(typeNode).kind)) <> "TYPE_REF" Then` — FreeBASIC's `Or` does NOT short-circuit (only `OrElse` does, per this codebase's own established convention). When `typeNode = -1` (always true for a non-array DIM'd variable, e.g. `AS LIST`), the right-hand side still evaluated `ps.ast.nodes(-1)` — an out-of-bounds crash (`Aborting due to runtime error 6`) that fired the instant `FOR EACH x IN someListVar` was lowered to MIR, before ever reaching the (correct, already-written) declared-type rejection check a few lines later in `MIREachSingleArrayInfo`. Fixed: `Or` -> `OrElse`. This crash blocked the MIR interpreter/native x64 path entirely (see below) even for the deliberate "reject cleanly" case.
62	    2. **LIST_NEW/DICT_NEW/SET_NEW had no return-type registration** (`src/type_binding/type_builtin_registry.fbs`) — same class of gap as CODEPTR/LPTR earlier this session. `DIM x AS LIST: x = LIST_NEW()` failed with "assignment requires explicit cast TYPE_OBJECT to LIST". Fixed: added as rules 69-71 (canonical type = the literal string "LIST"/"DICT"/"SET" — this whole type family has no `TYPE_*` constant in `type_rules.fbs`, unlike PTR/STRING/etc., so the declared type and the constructor's registered return type both just pass through unchanged and correctly match).
63	    3. **The AST interpreter never actually wired up LIST_NEW/DICT_NEW/SET_NEW at all** — `ExecCollectionCreate` (the real, correct constructor, allocating a slot in `gExecCollections`) existed but had zero callers anywhere. Added `Case "LIST_NEW"/"DICT_NEW"/"SET_NEW": Return ExecCollectionCreate(...)` to the three existing category functions in `src/runtime/exec/exec_eval_builtin_categories.fbs` (`ExecEvalBuiltinCollectionList`/`Dict`/`Set`).
64	    4. **Two separate builtin-name whitelist gates in `src/runtime/memory_exec.fbs`** (`ExecIsBuiltinCallName` at ~line 1950, and the dispatch `Select Case` inside `ExecEvalBuiltinCall` at ~line 3202) both had to explicitly list `LIST_NEW`/`DICT_NEW`/`SET_NEW` or the call is rejected before ever reaching fix #3's new code — confirmed by hitting "exec: unsupported call LIST_NEW" twice more even after fix #3, each time from a different, earlier gate. Fixed both. **Lesson reinforced**: this codebase repeatedly gates a single builtin name at 2-3 independent, unsynchronized whitelist points (semantic type registry, `ExecIsBuiltinCallName`, the `ExecEvalBuiltinCall` dispatch Select Case) — when adding ANY new builtin, grep for ALL of these, don't assume fixing one is enough (this is now the second time this exact multi-gate pattern has bitten a fix this session, after CODEPTR).
65	  - **Verified empirically** (`run`, AST interpreter): LIST create/add/FOR EACH(item,idx)/DO EACH(item,idx) with correct ordinals; DICT create/set/FOR EACH single-var=key/FOR EACH(key,value) positional; SET create/add/FOR EACH single-var=member; a mutation-during-FOR-EACH test (body calls `LISTADD` on the same list being iterated) confirms true snapshot semantics (only the original 2 items are visited, total=3, not affected by the 2 appends made during the loop); a DO-EACH-with-mutation test confirms the loop bound is fixed at entry (exactly 2 iterations) even though the list grows inside the body, consistent with the existing single-array-variable DO EACH precedent. Regression-checked the existing array-EACH test, the P0 snapshot/JIT scalar test, and the CODEPTR test — all still pass unchanged after these four fixes.
66	  - **NOT done, deliberately paused pending a decision — MIR interpreter (engine #3) and native x64**: fixing bug #1 above unblocks the crash, but `FOR EACH x IN someListVar` still hits `MIREachSingleArrayInfo`'s deliberate rejection ("requires a concrete iterator contract") for the MIR path, because no MIR-level lowering exists yet for the collection case (unlike the array case's `MIRLowerArrayEachLoop`). Writing one is very doable (call `LISTLEN`/`LISTGET`-style MIR_CALL instructions in a real generated loop, mirroring the array lowering's block structure) and would make it work correctly on the MIR interpreter, which already has full LIST/DICT/SET support (`mir_interp_collections.fbs`). **The open question**: the *native x64* backend has ZERO opcode support for any LIST/DICT/SET operation today (confirmed: `LISTADD`/`LISTLEN` called directly by a user program already compile "successfully" to x64 today but silently misbehave at runtime via the generic, unrecognized-name `__uxb_rt_host_call4` bridge — the exact same class of bug CODEPTR had). Writing the collection-FOR-EACH lowering would extend this SAME pre-existing silent-failure gap to one more syntax form, trading today's honest compile-time rejection ("requires a concrete iterator contract") for x64 specifically for a "compiles fine, wrong/crashes at runtime" outcome — worse, not better, for that one backend, even though it would be strictly a net improvement for the MIR interpreter. This tradeoff needs an explicit decision (accept the parity-with-direct-LISTADD-usage inconsistency for now vs. finding a way to keep x64 failing closed) before writing the lowering — not decided yet.
67	- **CODEPTR x64 real routine address — DONE and empirically verified 2026-09-08** (Codex's UXGSL blocker, ownership taken via `ai_koordinasyon/SORULAR_CEVAPLAR.md`): `CODEPTR(routineName)`/`LPTR(routineName)` always produced 0 (or, discovered mid-fix, silently routed through a generic runtime host-call bridge that also just returns a fixed dummy value) instead of the routine's real code address — meaning a BASIC FUNCTION could never actually be used as a C callback (e.g. GSL's `gsl_integration_qag`). Two independent bugs, both needed fixing:
68	  1. **MIR lowering never had a case for CODEPTR/LPTR** (`src/semantic/mir_lower_expr.fbs`, `MIRLowerExprNode`'s `CALL_EXPR` handling): unlike `SIZEOF`/`OFFSETOF` (which have dedicated lowering), `CODEPTR(x)`/`LPTR(x)` fell through every specific case and got lowered as an ordinary function call — with `CODEPTR` itself as the (unresolvable) callee name — which resolved via the generic "unknown function name -> runtime host-call by name" path (`__uxb_rt_host_call4` in `native/uxb_runtime/uxb_runtime_mir.cpp`), printing `MIR host call is not bound: CODEPTR` and returning a fixed dummy value. Fixed by adding an explicit case that extracts the argument's raw identifier TEXT (not a lowered/evaluated expression — `CODEPTR(MyFunc)`'s argument is a routine name, not a variable read) and emits a dedicated `"CODEPTR"`/`"LPTR"` MIR instruction.
69	  2. **The x64 emitter's existing CODEPTR/LPTR/ADDR_OF handler only tried "is this a local variable's stack offset"** (`MIRX64EmitAddressLikeOpcode` in `src/codegen/x64/mir_x64_opcode_surface_emitters.fbs`) and silently stored `0` for anything else — meaning even with bug #1 fixed, a routine name (not a local variable) would still resolve to 0. Fixed by adding a fallback: scan `cg.modulePtr->functions(...)` by name (same linear-scan pattern as the existing `MIRX64FindUserFunctionIndex`) and emit `lea rax, [rel <MIRX64FunctionLabel(name)>]` using the SAME label-naming convention already used for real `CALL`s — so a CODEPTR'd routine and a normally-called routine always agree on the same address. Only a name matching neither a local variable nor a declared SUB/FUNCTION now errors clearly, instead of silently producing 0.
70	  - Also fixed a **prerequisite semantic-layer gap**: `CODEPTR`/`LPTR` had no entry in the builtin return-type registry (`src/type_binding/type_builtin_registry.fbs`, `UXBBuiltinTypeRuleAt`) — every use fell through to a generic `TYPE_OBJECT`, making `DIM p AS PTR: p = CODEPTR(x)` a compile error ("assignment requires explicit cast TYPE_OBJECT to TYPE_PTR"). Added both as `TYPE_PTR`/`"IDENT:1"` rules (rule count bumped 67→69), matching the existing `VARPTR` entry's shape exactly.
71	  - **Verified empirically** with a self-contained native x64 test (no external DLL needed): `CODEPTR(MyFunc) <> 0` (real address, not zero), calling `CODEPTR` on the SAME routine twice yields the SAME address (stable), and `CODEPTR` on two DIFFERENT routines yields DIFFERENT addresses — all three checks pass after the fix (all three silently passed-but-wrong, giving a constant dummy value for every routine, before it). Regression-checked FOR EACH/array-iteration (`toplam=150 idxToplam=10 breakToplam=30 legacyToplam=6 doToplam=150`) identical across `run`/`--interpreter-backend MIR`/native x64 after touching the shared `mir_lower_expr.fbs`/`mir_x64_opcode_surface_emitters.fbs` files — no regression. **Not yet verified**: the actual real-world GSL callback end-to-end (`tests/libraries/uxgsl/uxgsl_basic_callback_smoke.uxb`, written by Codex) — this compiles cleanly now (was failing at the semantic-gate step before this fix) but fails at FFI-resolve time (`GetProcAddress ... symbol=uxgsl_matrix_create not found`) because the currently-deployed `bin/uxgsl.dll` is stale relative to Codex's in-progress `libsx/uxgsl/uxgsl.bas` (v101-era DLL, v104-era source) — this is Codex's active work-in-progress deployment, not a CODEPTR bug; reported back to Codex to redeploy and confirm.
72	- **FOR EACH / DO EACH deep dive + engine-map CORRECTION (2026-09-07)**: user pasted a long ChatGPT-authored analysis of FOR EACH/DO EACH; asked to verify it against real code and plan (discussion-only turn, no code changed yet — explicit "planlayalim, tartisalim... gorevlere geri donulecektir").
73	  - **Correction to the BYREF entry above**: that entry said `mir_evaluator*.fbs` "turned out to be used only by the YAMA6 slot/event/thread/paralel runtime surface" — **this was wrong, now disproven by exhaustive grep**. `MIRRunModule`, `MIRInvokeUserFunction`, `MIREvaluateInstruction`, `MIRSlotTriggerEntry`, `MIRHandleSlotBuiltinCall` all have **zero callers anywhere outside their own file cluster** (`mir_evaluator.fbs` + `_tail`/`_tail_controlflow`/`_tail_rest`/`_memory_helpers`). `mir.fbs` merely `#include once`s it (makes it compile, doesn't call it). Real YAMA6 SLOT/EVENT/THREAD/PARALEL handling is done independently by (a) `src/runtime/exec/exec_slot_manager.fbs` for the AST interpreter, and (b) `mir_interp.fbs`'s own `Case "SLOT_DEF"/"SLOT_BIND"/"TASK_TRIGGER"` handlers (~line 695-772) for the canonical-MIR interpreter — each engine reimplements this independently. So `mir_evaluator*.fbs` is genuinely dead code, same class as the AST-interpreter cluster below. The earlier BYREF fix applied to `mir_evaluator_tail.fbs`'s `MIRInvokeUserFunction` was real, correct work, but on unreachable code — harmless, not currently exercised.
74	  - **Full, verified engine/backend map** (answers user's "4 engines, 2 MIR interpreters, where did the 2nd come from" question): there are **4 LIVE execution/codegen forms** plus **2 fully dead clusters**.
75	    - LIVE #1 — AST interpreter: `src/runtime/exec/*`, entry `ExecRunMemoryProgram` (`memory_exec.fbs`). Used by `run` (default) and the AST side of `--interpreter-backend BOTH`. Confirmed via direct read of `main_program_entry_part2.fbs:49`.

---
name: uxb-fix-plan-decisions-2026-09
description: "Standing workflow rule + running log of the user's decisions on which uXBasic compiler issues (from audit Reports I-III) to fix and how."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 760ce433-ff72-46c7-8b20-30eed40f7a8c
